title: Filters list
description:
List of filters to apply for pixel selection on spectra.
 Example: we want to select the pixels for which 
 1. flag corresponding to 8 is absent 
 2. flag corresponding to 4 is present or flag is 0 : 
 [{"key": "Flag", "instruction": "^", "value": "8"}, {"key": "Flag", "instruction": "0&", "value": "4"}]

anyOf.title: Filter byValue
anyOf.description: A filter by value specifies a column name available in the input spectrum, a comparison operator and a constant value to compare with.

key.title: Column name
key.description: Name of the spectrum column to filter on

instruction.title: Comparison type
instruction.description:
* **in**: value must the be a list of possible value 
 * **~in**: not in 
 * **!=**: different 
 * **& / ~&**: binary and / not binary and 
 * **0&**: binary and or 0 
 * **^ / ~^**: xor / not xor

value.title: Value to compare with
value.description: Possible values are int - float - list of numbers (for `in` and `!in` only)

anyOf.title: Morphology Filter
anyOf.description:
Morphology filter is used to apply a bitwise morphology operation on the combined mask obtained by the application of all the previous filters in the list. It can be used to remove isolated pixels left after masking by the other filters or to enlarge or shrink the mask. For instance : 
 * To remove isolated pixels, use 'opening' [1,1] 
 * To enlarge mask by one sample use 'erosion' [1, 1, 1]

instruction.title: bitwise morphology operation
instruction.description:
By convention the mask, deduced from the previous filters, flags bad samples with 1 and good samples with 0. 
 * **erosion**: shrinks ranges of contigous bad pixels (a kernel [1,1,1] for removing one pixel)
 * **dilation**: enlarges ranges of contiguous bad pixels
 * **opening**:  an erosion followed by a dilation, removes small spots of bad pixels
 * **closing**: a dilation followed by an erosion, connects near ranges of bad pixels
